mapName: A Learnable Russia - No Car Metas - All

metas.name: Altai landscape
metas.note: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north through the Altai Mountains, often with foggy or rainy coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Bashkir bilingual signs
metas.note: Bashkir bilingual signs are found in Bashkortostan and use “урамы” for street, the same as Tatar, but are often not abbreviated.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Bilingual town names
metas.note: Some republics of Russia with minority languages use bilingual town entry and directional signs, such as in Bashkortostan and Tatarstan displaying Bashkir and Tatar respectively.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Black poplar
metas.note: The black poplar is commonly found south, near the border with Ukraine, as well as toward the western border with Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Black traffic sign bottom
metas.note: This black traffic sign bottom is primarily found in Stavropol and Chechnya, as well as western Dagestan. Rarely, exceptions can be found in other southern federal subjects such as Kabardino Balkaria, but these will typically be uncolored.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Blue-pod lupines
metas.note: Blue-pod lupines appear very commonly in northern Vladimir Oblast, eastern Ivanovo Oblast, and southwestern Kostroma Oblast. It can also be found less commonly elsewhere in Kirov Oblast and towards the Baltics.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Buryatia haze
metas.note: This forest fire haze is found near Lake Gusinoye, southwest of Ulan-Ude in Buryatia. While similar to the haze found near Mirny, the Buryatia haze coverage can typically be recognised by the open rolling landscape, which is not found near Mirny.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Buryatia landscape
metas.note: The landscape in Buryatia is very unique, containing open grassy landscape with shrubs and mountains. It is lusher near Baikal, but the mountains persist.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Caucasus mountains
metas.note: The Caucasus mountain range is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, Mount Elbrus, can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Chuvash bilingual signs
metas.note: Chuvash bilingual signs, found in Chuvashia, use “урамӗ” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Clips on signposts
metas.note: Clips on edges of signposts are found in Leningrad and St. Petersburg, and very rarely in Pskov, Novgorod or elsewhere.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Clustered birches
metas.note: Birches very close together, as well as forests consisting of only birches, are indicative of areas east of the Urals, most commonly between Chelyabinsk Oblast and Novosibirsk Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Cobblestone pavement
metas.note: Cobblestone pavement is notably common in Kaliningrad, Nizhny Tagil in Sverdlovsk, and Kizel in Perm Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Concrete block roads
metas.note: As you go further north in Russia, some roads are made out of several concrete blocks. It is notably common in the Komi Republic, Nenets, and Yamalo-Nenets.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Cyrillic and latin town names
metas.note: Town names written in both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets are common near the Baltic border and around Moscow, and to a lesser extent in federal subjects on the Finnish border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Dagestan landscape
metas.note: Grassy fields, with bushy vegetation, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely flat or mountainous. These flowers are also quite common in the Generation 4 Dagestan coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Desert steppes
metas.note: The area west of the Caspian Sea can often be recognised by its extremely dry and flat landscape, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan Oblast, and Dagestan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: East of Birobidzhan
metas.note: On the east side of the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, the coverage turns from rainy to wet after the rain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Eastern bollard
metas.note: Russian bollards that appear very thin and attached to a stick are usually found in the eastern part of the country, starting around Omsk. Note that ordinary Russian bollards are still plentiful in this part of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Extended insulator bars
metas.note: Extended insulator bars on poles are notably found in southern Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast, as well as southern Kemerovo Oblast. Edit from Vincent: Can also be found in Petrozavodsk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Far north
metas.note: The landscape in the far north can be recognised by the relatively flat landscape, with very low vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Fireweed
metas.note: Large amounts of the pink or red flower fireweed (Chamaenerion angustifolium) typically indicates a northern region of Russia. Similarly, most places north of Moscow commonly have fireweed.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Kamchatka landscape
metas.note: The Kamchatka peninsula has unique grey gravelly soil, as well as the largest number of volcanoes of any region in Russia. They are frequently seen across the peninsula, and in some places can appear quite close such as in Klyuchi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Karelia and Murmansk rocks
metas.note: Rocks along the road are extremely common throughout most of Karelia and Murmansk Oblast. They can also be found in Perm Krai and Buryatia but are less common and smaller in size.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Khabarovsk-Vanino road
metas.note: The Khabarovsk-Vanino road has a mountainous landscape with very sunny coverage. It also drives west with a black car with a blurred, long antenna, which helps to confirm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Kolyma Highway
metas.note: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall hills and mountains, usually shrouded in a haze. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature dark gravelly soil. The haze is not present in the western half.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Komi bilingual signs
metas.note: Komi bilingual signs, found in the Komi Republic, use “улича” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Limestone brick
metas.note: Buildings made of white limestone brick are indicative of Dagestan, as well as adjacent regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Lined oak trees
metas.note: Lined oak trees, often with a single white stripe around the trunk, are extremely common in Kaliningrad.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mari bilingual signs
metas.note: Mari bilingual signs, found in Mari El, use “урем” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mari El historical buildings
metas.note: Historical buildings in Mari El often have a unique architecture style. You will frequently see design patterns that include green roofs, red brick sprinkled with white stone details. Local churches commonly feature a similar style.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mesh framework utility poles
metas.note: Utility poles with a mesh framework are usually found in Petrozavodsk, but can much less commonly be found in cities like Tolyatti.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mosques
metas.note: While mosques can be found everywhere in Russia, they are by far most common in areas with a Muslim majority, mainly in much of south Russia as well as Tatarstan and Bashkortostan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Murmansk landscape
metas.note: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and fireweed usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Northern Sakhalin
metas.note: The road to Okha in northern Sakhalin is unpaved, revealing its very sandy soil. The road is surrounded by short, stunted bushes and trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Olkhon Island
metas.note: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling sandy hills during sunset. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Omsk landscape
metas.note:
The coverage in Omsk Oblast is some of the most recognizable in Russia. It is typically summer Generation 4 and has a distinct landscape consisting of green agricultural fields, which are interrupted by isolated patches of (primarily) birch forest.

Note that in Generation 3, this landscape can be seen in a much larger area of Russia.

NOTE: This combination of coverage and landscape spills over slightly into the neighbouring Tyumen and Novosibirsk Oblasts (in the south, and near Tatarsk, respectively).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Outer dashed road lines
metas.note: Outer dashed road lines are usually found throughout Kursk Oblast. An exception can be found in Tuva Republic. Rarer exceptions include the Republic of Karelia, Primorsky Krai and Khabarovsk Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Poorly-tracked dirt roads
metas.note: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Red brick
metas.note: Buildings built almost entirely of red brick are mostly found south, but other notable exceptions include Magnitogorsk, Orsk, and Omsk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Red soil
metas.note: Red soil is common in the highlighted areas, notably around Izhevsk and Perm, much of Arkhangelsk Oblast, Leningrad Oblast, and Pskov Oblast, and near Volgograd and Astrakhan. Note that this map is by no means exhaustive; red soil can be found almost anywhere in the country near water or iron mines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Road to Yakutsk
metas.note: A presence of Siberian larches and large mountains on a mostly paved, but sometimes wide-gravel road indicates the main road south of Yakutsk, with Generation 4 white car appearing north of Berkakit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Rounded rectangular fences
metas.note: Rounded rectangular fences with a line through the middle are unique to Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russian olive
metas.note: The Russian olive is typically found along the Kazakhstan border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sakhalin cabbage
metas.note: Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as Sakhalin cabbage) is very common in Sakhalin Oblast, particularly in the southern half. Related plants can very rarely be found in Adygea.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sandy roadsides
metas.note: Sandy roadsides are common in Khanty-Mansi and Yamalo-Nenets and adjacent subjects, as well as areas around Nizhny Novgorod on the Volga river. Other notable areas are Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha. Beware, however, that sandy roadsides can less commonly be found near rivers in other regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Siberian larches
metas.note: Siberian larches are one of the dominant tree species in much of eastern Russia, recognized by their unique needle-like leaves. Generally speaking, they become more prevalent the further east you go in the country, as well as at high elevations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Steering wheel on the right
metas.note: Japanese-made cars with the steering wheel on the right become more common the further east you go, generally starting around Novosibirsk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sunflowers
metas.note: Sunflowers are common along the border with Ukraine as well as more eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sunset coverage
metas.note: Sunset coverage, with the sun very close to the horizon, with an eastern-looking landscape will be the P-297 in Amur Oblast, roughly between the towns of Never and Sivaki.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tatar bilingual signs
metas.note: Tatar bilingual signs use “урамы” (ур., abbreviated) for street instead of “улица” and are unsurprisingly found in Tatarstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tropical plants
metas.note: Tropical plants in Russia such as palm trees are only found on the Black Sea, most commonly around Sochi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tunkinsky National Park
metas.note: Tunkinsky National Park in western Buryatia is a very green river basin with tall, jagged mountains to the north. In comparison to most of Buryatia, it is much greener.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tuva landscape
metas.note: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna will usually indicate the Tuva Republic. The south part of the main road in the Altai Republic and Tuva can appear similarly dry, so things such as driving direction and cloudiness can be used to distinguish them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Unique bollard
metas.note: This unique bollard, with a grey rectangle and double red reflectors, is specific to the P100 in Kostroma Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Very hazy coverage
metas.note: Very hazy coverage is found east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river. The colour of the haze varies, but it is often orange or white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Vladivostok area
metas.note: Lush and diverse forests in a hilly landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open rolling hill landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: West of Birobidzhan
metas.note: The Jewish Autonomous Oblast effectively has one road of coverage, outside of Birobidzhan. The west side has highly rainy and foggy coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: White flower
metas.note: This type of white flower (heracleum sosnowskyi) is most commonly found around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Yellow bands
metas.note: On the main road of Murmansk in generation 4, as well as some roads in Karelia covered in 2018, the vast majority of signposts will have two yellow bands wrapped around them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Yellow pole plates
metas.note: Yellow pole plates attached by a metal band are commonly found in Tatarstan. They are found on the majority of poles, but not all.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.
